utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in this courtroom and also those assisting us just outside the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Madam Registrar. May I first inquire in -- as to whether the exhibits, a list of 141, have been already introduced in the system or -- it's quite a lot of work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm informed that Madam Registrar has worked hard on it, but that not every single document has been assigned a number. So we'll hear from her most likely later today. Mr. Emmerson, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am insofar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, then you'll now be cross-examined first by Mr. Emmerson, who's counsel -- you don't -- I do understand that you don't hear me in -- there seems to be -- Madam Usher, could you please assist the witness in finding the right channel, perhaps. Mr. Zyrapi, do you now hear me in a language you understand? Now, Mr. Zyrapi --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, now I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- before I will invite Mr. Emmerson to start his cross-examination, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I should indicate insofar as I may need to refer to any of the documents that were formally produced yesterday, we have hard copies in a small clip. I don't think Your Honours have it. What I've done is I've made selections of the documents that I need to refer to, and I will also give what I hope is the correct at least Rule 65 ter number at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I'm going to ask you some questions on behalf of Ramush Haradinaj. I want to start, if I can, please, by just getting the basic chronology of your own personal involvement clear. Do I have it correct that between mid-March and the 28th of May, you were in Albania?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then between the 28th of May and mid-July, you were in Kosovo travelling around. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could both microphones of the witness be switched on, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They do both appear to be switched -- sorry, both of the microphones do appear to be switched on. If there's a problem --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: They weren't. Now they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then in mid-July, you were given a post of director of the operational department. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And prior to that, had you had a formal position, a title?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already mentioned yesterday, I was an officer for the development of the KLA in the framework of the operational directorate.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then from November 1998 until April 1999, you were Chief of the General Staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then in April 1999, you returned to Albania. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after I received another appointment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I want, if I may, to focus for a short time on the period between mid-March when you arrived in Albania and the 28th of May when you entered Kosovo. First of all, can I ask you this: You've told us that you were living in a flat with Naim Maloku and others. Was there a headquarters building in Albania at that time, between the 28th of -- I'm sorry, between mid-March and the 28th of May?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, at that time there wasn't a separate building for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was there a physical location in which the logistics department was based?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people I worked with at the time lived in different places.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And had meetings in their flats and cafes and so forth. Is that what you're describing for the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where they held that meet -- their meetings. I only met them when they came to my flat and took me to go and visit places.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So did you have a title yourself before you left Albania?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us that when you first arrived in Albania, there was a period of time you had to wait before being accepted by the General Staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And roughly how long was that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From mid-March until the 28th of May, when I joined, that was the period I was in waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you told us yesterday you spent some time training people inside Albania. Were you then not accepted into the KLA by that point?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was engaged logistically, but I hadn't received a confirmation from the General Staff that I had been accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yeah. Just so that we can get this situation clear, because it might have appeared yesterday in your evidence that there was some kind of organisational formality about all this. But from what you're telling us now, you were in a situation where you were neither in the KLA or out of it and yet being trusted to conduct training. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was the General Staff supposed to approve the membership of everybody who was admitted to the KLA or only people who had formerly held rank in the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The approval by the General Staff had to be given to the former officers who had served in the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So ordinary foot soldiers, if I can put it that way, people just turning up and volunteering, they didn't require any sort of formal approval by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so that I'm clear what you mean by that answer, ordinary foot soldiers -- dealing with ordinary foot soldiers who had not been officers of the Yugoslav Army, was it necessary for the General Staff individually to approve each and every one of them or not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, only the officers had to be approved, not the other people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Pardon, you mean the officers -- former officers of JNA or officers of KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was speaking about the former officers of the JNA and all the other armies as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: This is how I understood it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So they needed, if I can put it this way, to check you out. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only me, but all other former officers before they were allowed to join.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Like "you" as in --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the plural.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand your answer and I wasn't singling you out, but the point, if I can take it to the specific, in your particular case, the delay was about checking you out to make sure that you were reliable. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But even though they didn't know that you were reliable, they used you for training. Did that strike you as strange?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't start the training immediately. I started the training after some time I had been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that, but you've told us that you weren't approved until the 28th of May, when you left Albania. So from what you're telling us, you were being used for training even though nobody had finally come to the conclusion that you were safe.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I waited, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And who were these General Staff people?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, the members of the General Staff that I knew of were Xhavit Haliti and other people, Xhemal Fetahu, Ilir Konushefci, Raif Gashi. Azem Syla was as well involved at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were there some that you didn't know who they were?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were others as well, but I did not know all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you know who chose them to be members of the General Staff or whether they just chose themselves?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who chose them, because I wasn't there at the period; but when I went there, I met them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you ever learn who that group had been appointed by, if anybody, or whose authority they were -- on whose authority they were appointed?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the General Staff was formed by the LPK.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the process of choosing the members, do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness tell me what "LPK" exactly stands for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] LPK means the Popular Movement of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And, Mr. Emmerson, what was the meaning of your question: "The process of choosing the members, do you know anything about that?" Members of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, the members of the General Staff. If that wasn't clear, perhaps I should put the question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Wasn't that the gist of the answer before, what you were inquiring into?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I should put --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: The General Staff was formed by the LPK.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The question is the process by which the people were selected for membership, is the question I was asking. Let me -- let me put it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just for the sake of clarity, Mr. Zyrapi, but do you know anything about the process by which the individuals who were members of the General Staff when you arrived in March had been personally selected for membership of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, I don't know how people were appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At this point in mid-March when you first arrived, the General Staff, as far as you understood it, did it have any effective control on the ground of what was going on in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about any control at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The term "General Staff," as I said earlier, could create the impression of a degree of real organisation. So let me just ask you about that. You've told us as far as you know, is it correct, that they did not have a building out of which to operate?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And again, just to be clear, the General Staff, do you know how and where they would ever meet?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where they met and how they met.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I put this to you: From what you saw, is it fair to say that this was a group of men calling themselves the General Staff who were meeting in one another's flats and in cafes. Is that a fair summary of what was going on there when you first arrived?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I arrived there, I don't know where -- where and how they met. But when I arrived there, I told you that they came to my flat to see me, and they took me to the places where we did the training.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, one of the last answers of the witness was: "I don't know where they met and how they met." And then to summarize that, to say that they met in flats and cafes might not be a proper way of putting this --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm putting -- I'm putting a specific suggestion that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you said "Is it fair" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Is it a fair summary of what was going on? I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it suggests that it summarizes what the witness had seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When he said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or at least what he had told us what he had seen and it's not. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever see written documents whilst you were in Albania?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time I was in Albania, I never saw a written document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever understand anything about the structure of the operational department, as it was called? At that time, sorry.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time I was in Albania, no. I only knew about the logistics department.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And again, so that we're clear, the training that you were conducting, was that something that had been organised by somebody who called themselves a member of a logistics department or an operational department?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time I was there, it was the logistics department who undertook to do the training. I didn't know of any person who was in the operational department at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so that we have the picture clearly, somebody who said, I'm from the logistics department, asked you to do the training, is that right? An individual who said, I'm from the logistics department?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, he was in the logistics department. He introduced himself as such and he worked as such, and he asked me to get involved in the training of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Xhavit Haliti, but also Xhemal Fetahu and Ilir Konushefci.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were they also members of the logistical department?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Apart from meeting these men in your flat and doing what they had asked you to do, did you see any other evidence of a structure that might be called a logistics department: people, documents, places?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the time I was there, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, may I seek on one point of clarification from the witness. Mr. Zyrapi, you said: "I didn't know of any person who was in the operational department at the time." Now, in your statement of November 2005, you said: "In the early days of the war, spring 1998, the General Staff was composed of ...," and then you mention a few names. Among them, Rexhep Selimi, director of the military operations department. And then later on, you said that some members, and you specifically point at this Mr. Selimi, spent most of the time in Kosovo. How am I to reconcile that you say, I didn't know of any person in the operational department; whereas, in your statement you give this name, and you explain to us that this person was the director of the military operations department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. When I gave the statement in November 2005, I was explaining the phenomena and the way things happened, and part of those people I knew in Tirana, while the people in the operational directorate I got to know only after I entered Kosova, not during the period I was in Tirana.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you were giving a report looking back to the situation at that time, but not necessarily what you knew at the time. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I ask a question. Would you, Mr. Emmerson, intend to go into this procurement --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- process which the witness described yesterday? Because that may gain some evidence on the structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have some questions in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just follow-up on Judge Orie's question for a moment. As far as you know, during the time that you were in Albania, between mid-March and the end of May, were any members of the General Staff inside Kosovo at that time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I didn't know the names at the time, who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you know whether they were, in fact, involved in any of the combat operations or activities?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because there were, during that period of time, pockets of KLA activity in different parts of Kosovo as well as villagers beginning to arm themselves, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you did hear about them. You gave some answers yesterday about particular engagements, armed engagements, that you'd heard about?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: None of this was being coordinated by the General Staff, I suggest.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I then come to Judge Hoepfel's question and the issue of procurement of weapons. You yourself were involved, you told us, in inspecting certain weapons. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can I ask you: Who asked you to do that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked to do that by Xhavit Haliti, Xhemal Fetahu, Ilir Konushefci, Raif Gashi, and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And what sort of places would you go to look at these weapons?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked to go and inspect in Tirana, Elbasan, Durres, Shkoder.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Let me put the question a bit more specifically. Would you be going to a warehouse or would you be going to somebody's back garden? What sort of places would you be going to look at?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were in private places. They weren't warehouses. I just went there to inspect the weapons, whether they were fit for use.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say "private places," do you mean in people's homes?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And are we talking about you looking at quite small quantities at a time then, 10 or 15 weapons at a time, or much, much more than that on each occasion?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended. Sometimes there were small quantities, sometimes there were up to 50 or 100 weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So how small would the smallest quantities be that you might be asked to look at?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the smallest quantity was 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Just -- sorry, just to be clear. A moment ago, you said: "Sometimes there were small quantities, sometimes there were up to 50 or 100." Were there occasions when you, in fact, looked at much smaller quantities than 50?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There might have been, but I can't remember exactly. I remember more these quantities of 50 or a hundred weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is it right to say that very often these would be second-hand weapons?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And sometimes an assortment of different weapons brought together?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you have to examine them to see whether each individual weapon worked?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this was done also by other former officers who were there together with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And sometimes did you have to reject them because they were not functioning or poor quality or too old?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were quite a lot of them weapons that had been manufactured in the 1950s and the 1960s?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And these are really elderly pieces of kit, aren't they, for a modern army?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But it was just the best you could all get your hands on at the time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you started this line of questioning with referring to inspection of weapons the witness told us about yesterday. Could you give us the precise source, because I see some of this, but could you tell me exactly what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In terms of the witness's testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm afraid I haven't got the transcript line, but I'm sure we could find it enough --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you could please find it for me and then for me to put it in context.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Can we understand that this inspection was the preparation of the purchasing of these weapons? This was, how I understood it yesterday, that this was a process of purchasing this weaponry? I understood it correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And I would have one question in relation to that, but I don't want to interfere --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think Judge Orie may have a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'd like to hear the exact source, Mr. Emmerson, from you soon, the source of the testimony yesterday --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which page and which line? Then please proceed at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I've slightly lost my train of thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would there be occasions when you would take weapons that needed to be repaired but could be put in working order?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps already for the time being. You were talking about inspecting weapons. Were those weapons that were already in the possession of the KLA or the General Staff, or were those weapons that still had to be acquired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were weapons which had to be obtained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I think you'll find, just to be of assistance, I think you'll find the transcript - or at least part of it - pages 42 and 43 of yesterday's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's the passage -- on the uncorrected transcript, it's 42 and 43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in particular 42, lines 10 to 25, where the witness said he participated in the purchase of weapons and checked the technical part of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I just wanted to be sure that where the word "inspection" is used, that was also at a later stage somewhere else. So I wanted to be sure --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that when you talked about inspection of weapons, that you were talking about the checking of weapons --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Prior to purchase at this stage. Yes. That's what he's referring to at that part of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- it's clear to me now in the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to come very briefly to a matter that you referred to in your witness statement and very briefly alluded to in your evidence which was the first occasion that you came across Ramush Haradinaj in Tirana. Now, I want to be clear about this, if I can, with you. Is it right that you arrived back at your flat on one occasion as Mr. Haradinaj was leaving after he had been having a rather heated discussion with Naim Maloku. Is that a fair summary of the position?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And he was wounded at the time, I think, both in his hand and in his leg. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: His hand was bandaged and he was walking badly. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, first of all this: You referred very briefly yesterday to an attack on Gllogjan by the Serb forces, just a brief reference at one point in your evidence. Did it become clear to you that Mr. Haradinaj had sustained those injuries in the major assault that took place on Gllogjan on the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the time, but I learned from my colleagues that there were fightings in Gllogjan and that he was wounded during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you learn from your colleagues that he had come to Albania partly for medical treatment and partly to obtain further weapons to fight back?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard from my colleagues that he came for treatment to Tirana.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, again just to put it in summary form, did you discover from Naim Maloku that the basis of the disagreement was that Mr. Haradinaj was saying if there were trained soldiers in Tirana, we need you to help us in Kosovo, not to be sitting in Tirana?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I want to see if you can help us to date this meeting, because in your November 2005 witness statement, paragraph 8, you describe it as having occurred around the end of April or the beginning of May. I want to see if I can try and focus you down a little bit more on that. You're aware, aren't you, that Naim Maloku subsequently entered Kosovo on the 21st of April. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the accurate date when he joined. I don't recall the exact date. It may be around the date when he met with Ramush.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you remember a situation a little after this meeting when Naim Maloku went to Bajram Curri in preparation for being deployed into Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you remember him telephoning you in Tirana, that is Naim telephoning you in Tirana, when he was in Bajram Curri, and asking you why you, yourself, weren't there with him?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this conversation, but I know that he -- I remember that he called me from Bajram Curri; this is how far I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was there a discussion between you about whether he should come back to Tirana or go ahead to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that we had a conversation, but I don't remember the contents of that conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. You remember the phone call, and you remember that Naim Curri was in -- sorry, Naim Maloku was in Bajram Curri at the time of the phone call. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can you confirm that it was on the same night as the phone call that Naim Maloku entered Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the accurate time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I know that we had that phone call.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let me put it to you this way. You accept, do you, that the 21st of April could be the right date?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain about the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Can you help us with this: How long before that phone call, roughly, was the occasion when you saw Ramush Haradinaj in Tirana?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well, very well. I'll leave it then. I'll leave the question then. I want to come now to what you see when you enter Kosovo, what your understanding is of the state of organisation inside Kosovo at the time. And for that purpose, I want to put to you a passage of the testimony that you gave in the Limaj trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I wonder if we might have that on the screen. This is document identification 1D110714, that is the start of Mr. Zyrapi's testimony, and the passage I want to ask him to look at is 0719. It should have, yeah, 6823 at the bottom. Could we look, please, to line 24, first of all, on that page, and I want to then follow the text through from there. So I'll just read this into the record, if I may. The bottom of page - and we're now in the Limaj transcript - 6823, line 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say this: "At the time of my arrival, there were two active zones where combat was going on and which had organised units. At that time, it was," and then we need to go over to the following page, "it was Drenica zone, which was in the phase of development, and the Dukagjini Plain Zone, which was also active in military actions and in its development. "Q. Now, I'm just going to concentrate on those two for the moment. Were the -- those two zones developed in the same way or were they being developed differently, at different stages, and so on? Can you describe what was happening? "A. Yes. These two zones, as I said, were in the phase of development; they were not fully developed. They had reached the level of organised units in villages and were moving towards the unification of the command of the Drenica zone. Gradually these units had started their structuring in military ways, like units and companies, and they were all directly linked to the command of the zone. Later on, the development of the command continued in the next period. "Q. And can you just indicate what the next period was from the point of view of months? Which part of 1998 are we dealing with for the next period?" And you say: "They continued into the next period, and in August of 1998 brigades emerged. It was easier to form brigades in the Drenica zone" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Reading usually goes quicker than --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Although they have the transcript to translate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, I'm following the interpreters also on other languages. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I'll pick up where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. You reply: "They continued into the next period, and in August of 1998 brigades emerged. It was easier to form brigades in Drenica zone because the territories had been designated, and the development of these brigades continued because in July, August, September, we suffered many offensives which caused an impediment to us to continue with the establishment of other zones." Well, question -- sorry, question. "Q. Well, that brings me to ask you about a zone we've heard about, namely Pastrik zone. What can you tell us about that and its development? "A. When I arrived in June, this zone was not developed as a zone. They were self-organised units, local staffs such as the local staff in Malisheve of not very high military organisation level. This zone began to be structured in mid-June. I don't know exactly the date, but I know that during my visits to this zone in this time, I came across many self-organised units and units that were not unified in the command. This zone was not active at that time. In June, the preparations for the zone began, and of course in June and July we couldn't reach the highest level of organisation of this zone. As I said, there were many Serb offensives in June and July. The restructuring, however, continued to the next months but it did not reach the desirable level, as was the case with other zones as well. "Q. When did it reach the desired level? "A. The level" -- and this is your answer, "the level of brigade or zone was not reached until the end of the war, but in those parts when this was achieved at a lesser level, it was in October or November. You could speak here of a small unification of command, of the military structure emerging, and then it continued in January and February, and with the beginning of the NATO bombing campaign the zones were consolidated and organised in military zones." Now, first of all, can I ask you to confirm that that is a correct assessment of the position as you understood it to be at the time that you had entered into Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So at that stage, is it right to say then there were only two zones, as such, that had been described as zones within the KLA; that is, Drenica and Dukagjin?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I explained this in my statement as well, I said that the Dukagjini Zone was more active in terms of attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I'm not criticising you; I'm just seeking clarification from you. Can you confirm that in the period after you arrived on the 28th of May, so we're now talking June and July, there were only two areas of Kosovo in which it -- there was what was described as a KLA zone; namely, Drenica and Dukagjin?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it wasn't until much later that the zones of Llap and Pashtrik and Karadak and so on came to be established, was it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. At least this is what I know. They were formed at a later time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And by "a later time," those zones didn't come to be formed as zones until the autumn, did they, of 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, they didn't function as proper zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you were also asked a question in the evidence that you gave in the Milutinovic case about zones, and I'm not going to go to the transcript because it's a shorter passage. But for the record, it's the Milutinovic transcript page 5967, line 19. You were asked to look at -- to address the position across the whole of Kosovo during the period that you were there after the 28th of May. And you were asked this question: "Now, just so we have the right understanding of this, did the KLA hold the entire territory within each zone?" And you replied: "No, no. Only a very little part of each zone." Now, can I understand, what is the position here? Is that -- is that an accurate reflection of the position?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So when we talk about zones, generally, are we talking about areas of operation within which there may be pockets of KLA control and pockets of Serb control?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, can I be clear, was that your understanding about Drenica?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In general, this applied to all the zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That was going to be my question. And so just so that this Trial Chamber has your testimony clear, was that also the position in relation to Dukagjin?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about the period I was there, from July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, just for you to know that I have some difficulties in understanding this testimony where it seems that the word "zone" is used both for a geographical denomination and for a -- and kind of an organisatorial [sic]. I mean, if you are talking about functioning of zones, if you're talking about establishing of zones, and if one or two questions later the reference to zones seems to be to a geographical area, that is -- at least there is a risk of confusion --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think, if I may say so, that -- that really lies at the heart of an analysis of this part of the testimony is teasing out the difference between an area of responsibility, being a geographical zone, and a zone command, being concentrated pockets of KLA activity within a more or less emerging command structure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is your explanation of it. I'm just pointing out what problems I'm facing at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to put a very specific suggestion to you about the Dukagjin Zone. I'll come back to look at some of the documents emanating from that zone a little later in your evidence, but I want to put a very specific suggestion to you. You have told us that when you went to Dukagjin in middle -- in the middle of July, the area to the west of the Peje-Gjakove road was not properly integrated into the Dukagjin Zone, and that the purpose of your visit was to improve that integration. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to suggest to you that the formation of what came to be described as the Dukagjin Operational Zone evolved over the period from the end of March to August with a smaller Dukagjin Staff being formed at the end of May out of the commanders of villages in the area of Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the earlier period, how they were formed, but it was like ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I want to suggest to you specifically that at the end of May, a smaller area covering a number of villages around Gllogjan came together to form a Dukagjin Staff, which included neither Junik on the west, nor Jablanica on the east.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For that period, I don't know what it comprised. I spoke only about the time I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. But you do know, I think, because you've been taken by the Prosecution through some of the documents that show the process by which the Dukagjin Zone enlarged, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't know that, because it was for the first time for me that I saw the documents put to me by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well, we'll look at them in a little more detail in a moment or two. Again, now I want to come back to the issue of the General Staff and its functioning whilst you were first inside Kosovo, so that we understand -- we've asked -- I've asked you some questions about the General Staff and what it really amounted to in Tirana, and now I want to ask you some questions about the General Staff and what it really amounted to on the ground once you had entered into Kosovo. Because by then, you've told us, you were admitted as a member of the KLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was it from the 28th of May that you also had the rank that you've described, or the title that you've described, within the operations department?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So can we take it that from that point onwards, you knew a little bit more about how the General Staff was trying to function or not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there a headquarters for the General Staff in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that when I entered, the headquarters was in Likoc --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure about the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- but the General Staff moved from place to place. They did not stay in one place only. That -- those movements were for reasons of security.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And -- again, just so the Chamber has it clear, whilst you were in Kosovo after the 28th of May, was the whole General Staff then in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Part of the General Staff was inside Kosovo, the rest was in Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And how many, roughly, of these individuals were in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the General Staff who was inside, such as Rexhep Selimi, Sokol Bashota, Jakup Krasniqi, Hashim Thaqi, who sometimes stayed inside Kosovo and sometimes left, Adem Grabovci was inside as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you've given us four names who were inside Kosovo continuously, is that right, and one name, Hashim Thaqi, who went backwards and forwards. Is that an accurate reflection of the position?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did these four who were there the whole time, did they stay together in one place? Sorry, let me rephrase that question. Did they stay together and move from place to place, as you have described, or were they in different locations?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember - because I was always on the move because of my operational duties - I know that the members of the General Staff were always in movement but not together.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So we've got four individuals, have we, in four different places?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying in four different places, but in several different places. I can't know where they all were because of the areas I visited myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand. But just so that we have the picture. They're moving about but they're not moving about together; that's what you've told us, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They still had no headquarters building in Tirana; is that the position, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember a building for that purpose in Tirana, at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to be clear, did they have a dedicated headquarters building in Kosovo, yes or no, in -- at the end of May/beginning of June?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of May and beginning of June, they were in Likoc, in the Drenica territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did they have a building there?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was that a building specifically set aside for the General Staff or did it do other things as well?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a private home.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So they were staying in somebody's home; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a private home; that's where the General Staff stayed in the period end of May/beginning of June, when I entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say -- as I said to you earlier, the concept of the General Staff and some of the labels and titles that you and your colleagues gave yourselves might create the impression that we were dealing with some sort of formalised military structure. But what you're telling us is the four individuals who were inside Kosovo and travelling around used to stay together in a private house from time to time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, if Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- I object to the way that question's framed. If the witness answers yes, the four individuals who were inside Kosovo -- if he answers yes to the notion of four individuals travelling around and staying together in a private house, that might imply that the impression that he's given about formalised military structures is also incorrect. It's -- it needs to be -- I certainly don't mind if Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- I don't mind if Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson understands the point and will take action accordingly. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think so that we're clear, perhaps if I put a subsequent question rather than invite the witness's response to what was a rolled-up question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When they travelled around then, did they have an escort that was dedicated to the General Staff or were they just using the guards that were already attached to the local village defence units to escort them from one place to the other, like you did when you visited the Dukagjin Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about their movements, how they were in the period of end of May/beginning of June. And I -- as I said, I moved on my own, so I don't know where the other members went.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you never see them the whole time you were in Kosovo from the 28th of May/beginning of June, right the way through to, let us say, the end of August? Did you not see them at all, yourself?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see them in July in Berisha, where the house was, and there were guards there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And you also saw them, I think, in mid-July because some of them came to Jablanica, you told us, with you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before going to Jablanica, I saw them. So I went to Berisha and then I went to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did some of them come to Jablanica with you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did they travel with their own dedicated protection unit, or did you use the services of the local villages in the areas you were coming across, to guide you from one place to another?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the movement of the General Staff to Jablanica was escorted by a number of guards, but they were part of the Berisha unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The Berisha unit. You mentioned you had seen them in Berisha. They were staying were they -- just so we're clear, Berisha is in the mountains area, isn't it? It's nowhere near Drenica?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So in mid-July you'd seen them in the Berisha area where there was a local KLA unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were they all together when you saw them in the Berisha area?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then you told us that they were accompanied to Jablanica by a group of soldiers from the Berisha area. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I put it to you this way: Were they borrowing the soldiers from the Berisha unit to take them to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "borrowing," but that was the unit that was guarding the General Staff there and that was the unit that escorted the General Staff to Jablanica as well -- a security unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where were they staying in Berisha?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, this was a private home close to the Berisha village in the Berisha Mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to put two specific propositions to you, which I think you've confirmed both in witness statements and in testimony you've given in the past. First of all, whatever the General Staff might have wished the position to be, zone commanders did not require or generally obtain the approval of anybody in the General Staff to engage in combat operations during this period, did they?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this particular period. I can speak about the July period.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, taking the period from the beginning of June through to the middle of July, I want to suggest to you -- and I have in mind, for example, paragraph 14 of your November 2005 statement, where you say that in practice zone commanders did not require the approval of the General Staff to engage in combat operations. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, not in that period, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All right. So that we're clear then. So the General Staff were not directing military activity of KLA units during the period we're concerned with between the end of May and middle of July --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have some difficulties with the way in which you reflect paragraph 14. You said: "In practice they did not require ..." "Require" is a normative expression; "in practice" is a factual expression. Paragraph 14, in my view, clearly states what was the norm and what was done in practice, and to mix -- to mix the two of them up is not something that further clarifies the issue. It talks about, in theory, what they had to obtain and what, in practice, they did obtain -- whether they did obtain. If you would replace the word "require" by "obtain" in your question, then I would have no problems anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm looking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said: "In practice they did not require ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry. I was just looking at the question to clarify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's paragraph 32 -- page 32, line 2: "In practice zone commanders did not require" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, I was looking at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say "did not request," then I would be less --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think we need to be clear as to who is requiring whom to do what, so let me put it this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The General Staff would have preferred the position to be a situation in which they were giving the orders for combat operations. That would have been the preference of the General Staff, wouldn't it? Simply answer that question first.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've used certain language in your statements, and I want to clarify what it means. You've - and I'll just read you the exact passage - you've said -- you've said this: "At the time, in order to carry out important combat operations, the forces on the ground, in theory, had to obtain the approval of the General Staff; however, in practice this was not happening. Until late 1998, it is an obvious fact that more power laid in the hands of the zone commanders than in the hands of the General Staff."

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now -- again, so that we're clear about the position, the -- when you say "in theory" combat operations had to be authorised, what do you mean by that, "in theory" they had to be authorised? Who decided that in theory, they had to be authorised by the four men travelling around Kosovo that you've described?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course the decision would have to be made by the General Staff possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, there wasn't any constitution at this stage that this General Staff had authority to issue instructions, was there?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that period, whatever -- what they had or didn't have. I can only speak about the period after July.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, when you say in that statement that they were in theory required, that is to say, that combat operations were in theory required to have the authorisation of the General Staff, on what do you base that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I base that suggestion on my knowledge that I have of proper armies, how they function, that the personnel have to act upon orders that are issued or approved by the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But this wasn't a proper army, was it, Mr. Zyrapi, at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that time it wasn't a proper army, a regular army. It was an army that was under development.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so. Maybe there would come a time when combat operations would be authorised by the General Staff, but at this point it was not the practice anywhere in Kosovo for any combat operations to be authorised by the General Staff in advance, was it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So there may be an implicit suggestion in that paragraph that there was something improper about combat operations taking place without the authorisation of the General Staff, or that might be one reading of the paragraph. But I'm asking you to clarify, from the last answer that you've given, that the position in practice on the ground between the end of May and, let us say, the end of July or, indeed, the end of August -- so, for clarification, the end of May to the end of August, is that no combat operations were ever authorised in advance by any of the four individuals describing themselves as members of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the periods in question, whether they were authorised or not. So I'm speaking about until July 1998. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. So you're -- the answer that you gave to us a moment ago, where you agreed with me that no combat operations were authorised by the General Staff in advance, relates to the period from the end of May to July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer I gave at the time was in general. For the period July/August, I know that not every operation was authorised.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we do need a little more clarity to this. I asked you a few moments ago to confirm that in the period we were considering from the end of May onwards, it was not the practice anywhere in Kosovo for any combat operations to be authorised by the General Staff in advance; and you said: "Yes, that is correct." Now, first of all, was that statement correct in respect of the period from the end of May to the middle of July?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said that, it was a general statement, not simply about the period May-July. This was an answer that comprised my knowledge about the period until September.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. So taking the general position from May until September, can you confirm for us, please, that combat operations were not authorised in advance by the General Staff anywhere in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And again, can you confirm, please, that there was no regular communication between the General Staff members and either the zone commanders or the lower levels of command?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, from July onwards there weren't regular communications between the General Staff and the zone commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say "from July onwards ...," can I be clear, does that answer apply from May to the end of September or only from July?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the earlier period, whether they met or how they met. I'm only speaking about the period where I -- when I was there until September.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All right. I'm sorry, there is some confusion in your answer. You were there from the end of May, and I'm asking you about the period from the end of May to September. In general, can you please confirm that from the end of May to September, there was no regular communication between the four individuals styling themselves members of the General Staff and either the zone commanders or any of those operating at a lower level in the village defences?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There weren't any regular meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think communication, generally, was difficult, wasn't it, between those four individuals and any of the commanders?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. In practical terms, it was difficult for any forms of communication to take place with the four members of the General Staff who were in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was very difficult to communicate at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just so that I can understand how the General Staff made its decisions, if it was making decisions, half of them were in Tirana; four of them were in Kosovo; and one, you've told us, was shuttling backwards and forwards. As far as you know, did they ever meet together to make decisions about anything during this period?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period, I don't think the members of the staff could get together in regular meetings --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and make decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So based on your experience -- I mean, a lot of the remarks that you make about how armies behave are based perfectly, properly on your experience of operating within an army. But to call this body a General Staff when it isn't meeting together and making decisions, has no effective authority to authorise combat operations, can't communicate with the commanders in the field, and is moving around from private house to private house, I mean, that's not a General Staff, Mr. Zyrapi, in any meaningful sense of the word, is it, at this period of time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period we're talking about, part of the staff was inside Kosovo, another part was outside Kosovo. So it was very difficult to come together and have unified decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It wasn't functioning as a General Staff in the sense in which that term is understood within military structures that you've previously been involved within regular armies, is it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, it wasn't functioning in the proper sense of the word. In normal armies, the General Staff would have the possibility to contact the troops and the commanders. But this was an army that was still a fledgling army, under development. So there wasn't a possibility to do all those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's exactly what I want to ask you because that word "fledgling" has been used by another military witness. Your job when you came in was to try and get some organisation together of what was happening on the ground. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the reality of the position on the ground, can you confirm this for me, is that there were pockets of people with guns who were calling themselves the KLA, organised primarily around villages initially?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during my visit. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And very often the man who had been the mayor of the village or the village leader would be elected as the KLA commander for that village. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there have been such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, it was quite common, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the period I have knowledge of, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And people would get together what scraps of uniform they could and any weapons they either had or could smuggle in from Albania and try to call themselves an army, at this point?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For that period, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then gradually over time in some areas, attempts were made to put those villages together into a coordinated command?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about the period from June, July, and onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And in fact, I'm going to suggest to you specifically that it wasn't until the 23rd of June that anything which can properly be called the Dukagjin Operational Zone came into existence by people coming together and agreeing to be part of a Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the earlier period or about June. I'm testifying here about the period from July onwards. It may have been as you said, but I wasn't informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But essentially, what you and others were trying to do was to help these, essentially, spontaneous village groups come together and organise and coordinate along some kind of structural lines that would make sense as a cohesive force; is that right, during this time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I don't mean what I'm about to say unkindly, Mr. Zyrapi, but will you please try to answer the question as objectively as possible. Part of that process involved giving people grand-sounding names like General Staff and chief of operations and logistics which were borrowed from real armies but which had no relationship at all to the reality of what was taking place on the ground?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the period we are talking about, June/July, they were all in place; but, as I said, the army was under development. Its structures were under development.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. The specific suggestion I'm putting to you is that part of the process of making these group of villages come together and look like an army was giving people big-sounding titles, drawn from real armies, like General Staff, when it reflected on the ground nothing that could properly be called a General Staff, for example?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the period I have a recollection of, it was called General Staff. But if you compare that to a General Staff of a regular army, of course the comparison wouldn't be proper because, as I said, it would be an army under -- in a process of development.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Finally on this, before we take a break, I'm going to just put it to you one more time. Giving people titles was part of the process of persuading them and the outside world that this could be brought together and made to look like an army, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Its intention was to develop and grow and become a regular army like any other army.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson, that would be. We'll have a break, Mr. Zyrapi, but I'll first ask Madam Usher to escort you out of the courtroom. We'll have a break of almost half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I, as always, have some concerns about the exhibits. I now see, referring to the November statement, that there are a few annexes which are in Albanian. I'm specifically drawing your attention to the documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Annexes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- mentioned, for example, in -- well, several paragraphs. For example, in 33 you find reference to a couple of documents. I would say the last ones attached, they're all in Albanian. Now, I do understand that English is the -- the English version of the statement is the originally filed document, signed by the witness. The attachments are, to some extent, in English but some of them are in Albanian. Now, if I look in the system, e-court system, then the original -- the translation would be the Albanian translation, which seems to be without attachments. That means that at least some of these attached documents, the last ones, we have them in Albanian but not in English. If the Chamber will have to evaluate this statement with the attached documents, then of course the Chamber would very much prefer to have them in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I don't see them attached to the translated version, or is this --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I think they must have been removed inadvertently. I can make arrangements for them to be -- for the Trial Chamber to be provided with translations as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so that we have -- we have access to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise for that. That won't be a problem. We can do that fairly quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because I see now that the translation is 16 pages, whereas it seems that the -- no, 15 pages, whereas the original, which is the English original, is 26 pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. I'll make sure that they -- they match and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- we'll send it out. I'll try and get that done either by the end of today, if Your Honours please, or if not, would tomorrow -- by tomorrow be okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you finish the --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'll try and get it done --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- witness, I would rather have it before the --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- witness leaves. We'll have a break until five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just one or two further questions, if I may, on the General Staff. I want to ask you some names, first of all, just to have them clear on the record. Azem Syla, A-z-e-m S-y-l-a, was he the main commander or the person describing themselves as the head of the General Staff at the time when you entered Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned this in July when I was appointed director of the operational directorate of the General Staff. The name that -- Azem Syla was the general commander of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if I can just put a number of other names to you and just check with each of them that they were members of the group calling themselves the General Staff at this point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, of course we have paragraph 15 of the November statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because what I heard until now is approximately the same. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I can do this briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Hashim Thaqi was one. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Rexhep Selimi?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Jakup Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sokol Bashota?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Xhavit Haliti?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They were all names that you knew as General Staff members?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was also Kadri Veseli, whom I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help me, did any of those individuals have any previous military experience as officers in any army?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none of them had any military experience from being previously officer in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the General Staff, so-called, was made up of individuals with no previous military experience?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to be clear, Azem Syla was a former university professor from the University of Pristina. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he did in the past.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. I'm going to suggest to you that Hashim Thaqi and Rexhep Selimi were students?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know either.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they were in the past or what they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you know what any of them had done in the past?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. And one other matter on an organisational topic. Can you confirm that nobody within the KLA was ever paid a salary or a wage?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know during the time I joined, they didn't get any salaries, they weren't paid.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did that remain the position throughout?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
