utterances.text: Now, coming to you and your own involvement, when you arrived you've told us that you were making visits to various villages and posts to check on the way in which weapons were deployed and people were organised. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And generally, is it fair to say that you encountered a poor level of military organisation in those villages?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to put to you a passage of the evidence that you gave in the Limaj case. I shall just read it because it's short but it's page 6834, line 21, and you're referring to the months of June and July 1998. And you said this: "At that time my visits were very short with every unit, and as to how they were organised I don't have full knowledge, not only for that particular area, which was Llapushnik, but for other areas as well." Again, can I ask you to confirm that that is an accurate reflection of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you were moving around very quickly from place to place?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Spending sometimes no more than an hour or two in one place?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember how much time I spent.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And there came a point, as you've told us, when you went to the Dukagjini area and to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, at this point, I want to pause in the narrative of your involvement and to look at some of the documents that the Prosecution have asked you to identify and comment upon that pre-date the period of your arrival in Jablanica; in other words, that deal with the evolution of the structures in that area during June and the early part of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So can I ask, please, first of all, that the witness be handed a copy of the yellow file of documents, which I think Your Honours already have on the desk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have received it on the desk. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I asked Madam Registrar to -- who has assigned to many of the documents one -- out of the 141 already numbers, to inform you and us about any document already in the system. So if you would please announce clearly what the number is, the ID -- the document identification so that Madam Registrar could tell us what number she has provisionally assigned to that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think if Your Honours cast an eye over the index, for example, items 1, 2, and 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- where we have been aware that a document identification number has already been assigned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- we have inserted that into the index.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may have come --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but if it comes to other documents, then let's see whether Madam Registrar -- and she'll certainly have a look at the list, I take it, Madam Registrar, to find out already whether any --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Further documents have been entered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- further provisional exhibit numbers have been assigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me try to bring it up-to-date as of this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The first document behind tab 1 which, I'll be corrected if I'm wrong, has already been given Exhibit P126 is document identification 1D111033. The Albanian is Exhibit P126, and the English translation 1D111033 at 1037. Now, first of all, Mr. Zyrapi, you -- if you look at the back of that Albanian original, do you see the name "Kompjuteri"?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is he there recorded as the minute-keeper?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the keeper of records.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And we'll obviously see these rough minutes at various points in similar handwriting. You've seen a number of documents in that handwriting, I think. Is that right? I'm sorry, you need to --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. So this is a document -- the minutes of a meeting headed the 8th of June of 1998. There's just one small passage of that that I wanted to ask you about. In the Albanian, can you see, please, at the bottom of the front page a reference to Rastavica, which in the English is two-thirds of the way down the front page? The way these are organised is Albanian first, and English translation after the immediate tab following.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if Your Honours can follow it in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you see a reference to Rastavica there where it is recorded that Banda e Madha has fallen. "They are trying to enter on foot and dressed in our uniforms."

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you become aware on your travels of occasions when Serb forces were dressing in KLA uniforms?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that period, and I have no information about this incident because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I understand that. I'm asking you as a general proposition whether that was something that you became aware of at any time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I became aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So can you help us as to when you first heard of occasions on which Serb forces would dress in KLA uniforms?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the accurate time, but from the time I started, that is, July onwards, I heard that they wore KLA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, you started, I think, at the end of May, Mr. Zyrapi, rather than from July onwards. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said at this period. I don't remember May. I never heard about it in May, because at the end of May I entered Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Every now and again, you say "from when I started, from July onwards." And I've understood your evidence to be that you started inside Kosovo from the 28th of May. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 28th of May, I entered Kosova, but I worked as an officer of the operational directorate. But in July, I started to have broader knowledge of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So was it from July, then, that you began to hear accounts of Serb forces wearing KLA uniforms?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if I remember right. Can't be very precise, but I do remember that when I visited these zones, I heard such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could now turn behind tab --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Rightly, you have often insisted on trying to explore the sources of knowledge of the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- could you please do that, and also try to find some more details about whether any specific incidents or of any specific events having been brought to the attention of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, can you tell us, please, how you learnt about occasions when Serb forces would wear KLA uniforms? Who told you? How did you find out? Was it something you saw yourself?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out during the visits I made to the units, to the zones, but also during fighting when I went to Rahovec, I saw with my eyes Serbian units - I don't remember whether they were police or national -- or army units - they wore Albanian national caps, and they approached the front line where the defence units of the KLA were.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And apart from the incident you, yourself, saw, you've told us that you learnt this when you were visiting different positions. Can you help us. Who would have told you when you visited the positions about Serb forces wearing KLA uniforms?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In general terms, would it have been other members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in general terms, would they be giving you these descriptions of incidents that had occurred within their general areas?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can you remember any -- apart from the Orahovac incident, can you remember any other specific incidents when this was brought to your attention, locations or dates or both?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the dates or places, but I do know that I was informed, I heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson. Could you tell us, do you remember when during fighting, when you went to Rahovec, when that exactly was that you personally observed Serbs wearing Albanian national caps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was when fighting had broken out in Rahovec. When I arrived there from Dukagjin, when I organised the Defence of the KLA positions from Rahovec in the direction of Malisheve, this occurred. This is when I saw what I mentioned on the road to Malisheve.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you have a month or a date for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was July, but I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think just to be clear, you'd already told us when you left Gllogjan you went to Jablanica and were called to Rahovec to witness the fighting there. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Gllogjan I went to Jabllanice where Lahi Brahimaj was waiting for me, and from there we went together to Rahovec --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was the same occasion where you received instructions from the General Staff to go there. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And so that we're clear then, the occasion you personally witnessed would have been in the middle of July?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. It may have been in second half of July or the end of July. Really, I don't remember the exact date when I saw that happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to then, to please, move to page -- tab 2 in this bundle in the Albanian tab 3 -- sorry, tab 2 in the bundle, which has the Albanian first and then the English. And for the record, the Albanian should, I think, be Exhibit 1 -- P129. The English translation is 1D111033 at 1041. Now, Mr. Zyrapi, again looking at the Albanian version, you can see the same minute-taker, I think. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that is the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I won't make an observation about the handwriting in those circumstances. Can you confirm that this is or records a meeting of the Gllogjan staff at Gllogjan on the 13th of June? If you look at the top of the document I think that's clear. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is written here that it's a meeting of the Gllogjan staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if you look at the second page of the document and you find the entry for HA, who I think appears to be somebody called H. Abazi, according to the record of those who were present. The English translation reads: "From what I understand the first step would be consolidation" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For Your Honours, I'm looking at the bottom of page 1 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to repeat, HA says: "From what I understand the first step would be consolidation. The second is the creation of the subzone within the framework of the Dukagjini Zone." And then RH is recorded as replying, after a word that is unintelligible: "RH ... is in favour of coordination, of the creation of single directing body. If we continue like this, with a multitude of staffs, it will be difficult." Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in your April 2007 statement, page 12, third paragraph, I'm going to read to you the comment that you made about that. You said this, and I'm quoting: "The document suggests that local headquarters operated independently but were eager to coordinate and unite into larger zones. The document contains a proposal to create a body or introduce other forms of management of the newly united headquarters of villages. Such meetings were common in many areas of Kosovo, and separate headquarters which acted independently met to consider consolidation or the creation of a leading body for various headquarters." Pause there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, the passage I have just read to you is from your own statement commenting on this document. Can I understand then from that, Mr. Zyrapi, that you saw this document as an example of a phenomenon that you had witnessed in other areas of village commands struggling in the beginning of June, and this is the 13th of June, to try to come together in some kind of coordinated command?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to illustrate the point, if we look behind tab 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, I'd like to -- Madam Registrar has some observations to be made about what we find under tab 2, which is P129. One minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar asks our attention for the following, Mr. Emmerson. These minutes are a two-page document, and it says: "English translation 1D11/1033," and that -- a translation is not attached to this Albanian original and is, most likely, a part of 65 ter document 147. So there is some confusion about the English translation where it comes from exactly and whether it's not part of a larger document. I'd like you to sort it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I know the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I'll be corrected from my right if I've got this wrong. The Prosecution created a document which was a continuous and single document of the translations of all of the documents that had been put to Mr. Zyrapi. Therefore, in order to have it coherent, this is an extract of what was a continuous translation of all of the documents, and the document identification number I have given you, 1D111033 at 1041 is a Defence document identification of that collective transcript and of the relevant page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I think the best solution would be to have that specific page where we find a translation of this specific document, that is the minutes from the meeting of the 13th of June, to attach that to the original --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so that we have them together.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Physically, that's what we've done in the bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In terms of the system, that's obviously something that can be done and if that's most convenient, it could be done once the evidence of the witness is concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that explanation, Mr. Emmerson. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, behind tab 3 -- sorry, can I indicate I was about to move on to a question which illustrates the point that you were making about the fact that even within the Dukagjin Zone, there were at that time different commands operating independently of one another. And I wanted to just turn behind tab 3, please. You have, I think, there the Albanian and we have the translation in this instance. This is Exhibit P128.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I hope I'm right in saying that the English translation for that one is directly linked on the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar will check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, can you confirm for us, Mr. Zyrapi, that this is an order the previous day to the minute you've just looked at; namely, the 12th of June, from a commander in Krushec? Mr. Zyrapi, can I ask you to confirm that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it's an order from a commander in Krushec; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This says: "In accordance with the order issued by the Isniq local staff to the defence staff in Krushec."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And at the top left-hand document, could you translate that, the very first line on the top left?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left, it says: "Krushec defence staff."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So are we to understand, this is a document addressed to the Krushec defence staff by the staff -- the local staff in Isniq?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can see in this document, this is an order by the local staff in Isniq sent to the Krushec defence staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to be clear, you know the difference between Isniq and Irzniq, don't you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Irzniq is another village.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Isniq is a little further north along the main road, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If you go from Gjakove, then you take the western direction towards Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. It's south of Peje between Peje and Decane, isn't it, Isniq?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Still within the Dukagjini area; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But here we have an order signed by a local commander, which I'm sure you can confirm is not signed by Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order is not signed by Ramush.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to turn now then, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I on the system look at P128 and if I then click on "source attachment translation" which is given a number 1D11/1057, if I click on that, my screen remains completely empty. So please -- would you please verify that the English translation is attached to it in the system as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Ours doesn't, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh. Then my computer is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may be that -- I don't know, does Your Honour have the B/C/S screen or the Albanian screen, rather than the English screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if you ask them for the translation, you should get the other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It certainly comes up when we click it on our screen and I think the registry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then it -- it will be my problem. And please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Tab 4 now, if we can, please. This is a document which I want to spend a little time on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can I indicate straight away, Your Honours, because it will become clear in due course, that there are two versions of the minutes of this particular meeting: a rough version which we're looking at here, and then a more detailed typed version which I'm going to need to pull up on the screen in a little while. But it's an important meeting and it's worth, if I may say so, looking at both sets of minutes, and I think the witness has looked at both sets of minutes in the course of his statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, first of all, Mr. Zyrapi, I want just to ask you, please, to quickly familiarise yourself with that document. You've looked at it before and you've commented on it before. It's a meeting - I suggest a very important meeting - on the 23rd of June in which the Dukagjini Operational Zone staff or the staff of the Dukagjini Operational Plain was established.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want, if I may, to put some passages to you from the translation. It's a little difficult for me to immediately find their corresponding position in the Albanian because of the way it's set out in the absence of line numbers, but I'm going to go through it in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if anybody wants to take a point about the accuracy of the translation, I'm sure that they will do so. But it's a Prosecution document, in any event. And so for Your Honours can I use the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We just can see the date of this meeting, can you confirm that, Mr. Zyrapi, at the very bottom of the page, the last line both on the original and the translation records this as a meeting that took place in Jablanica on the 23rd of June.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All right. And I want to just read to you certain passages and I'll give an indication to the Court which passages I'm referring to. Starting on page 1, the first entry is: "R. Haradinaj: Explained the organisational structure of the areas of competence of the staff of the Dukagjin area, so far divided up into six subzones. The purpose of the meeting: Coordinating participation, exchanging experiences, organisation, a single command." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just if you let your eye travel down a little further, you'll find an entry against the name of Salih Veseli. Yes? Do you know who --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know who Salih --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Do you know who Salih Veseli is?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Salih Veseli was one of the officers of the former Yugoslav Army, and when I went to the Dukagjin area in July, I met him there. He was Chief of Staff of the operational zone of Dukagjin.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that was in the middle of July?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So just coming back to the 23rd of June, the entry against the name Salih Veseli says this: "The people who are closer are those that understand one another. We have done something of great importance. No army has ever done" -- sorry, "has ever been" -- "no army that has ever been has done such a thing." Then this: "Some operations must be conducted. This can be done while uniting forces and leaders." And then a little further down, he says: "I think we must re-organise." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: A little further down from that, there's an entry against the name Major Salih, M-a-j-o-r S-a-l-i-h, where it says: "Major Salih read out the order for mobilisation dated 15th June." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then the minute records him saying: "I am in favour of forming an operational staff for the Dukagjin area so that we are in one command under a single roof. If we combine forces, we will deliver a powerful blow to the enemy." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then there is an entry under the name of Rrustem Teta. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you see a few lines down he says: "In my opinion," and the words "in my opinion" are underlined. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "In my opinion," he says, "there is little consolidation of forces." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just a few lines further down, he makes this proposal: "In order to proceed, we need coordination, a single command, in order to go forward. The soldiers I see are happier. Today is not time for ranks but only time to fight the enemy. We took a step forward when we formed the Dukagjin Staff." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you remember I suggested to you earlier that there was originally a much smaller Dukagjin Staff based around Gllogjan, and that it wasn't until the 23rd of June that what became known as the Dukagjin operational staff, expanding up to a wider area, was created. Do you remember me suggesting that to you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Will you bear that suggestion in mind as we look through these minutes because I'm going to suggest to you that what the minutes show is that this is a meeting in which that much smaller organisation was amalgamated with Jablanica into a single, much larger grouping, which became known as the Dukagjin Plain Operational Zone. Yes? So if I can just ask you to carry on with this, please. Can you look a little further down to the next entry against the name "Ramush Haradinaj"?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the third page?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look -- the entry that we've just looked at under the name "Rrustem Teta," do you have that, where he gives his opinion underlined? The top of the third page is the passage I want to ask your attention to, where the next entry against the name "Ramush Haradinaj" appears.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, he's recorded as saying this: "In order to help one another" -- I'm sorry. "In order to help one other in future, we have to supply the entire people with weapons, 16-year-olds and above." Pausing there for a moment. I think you gave evidence in the Milutinovic case that in relation to this particular line, that would have been an impossibility. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: An ambitious objective, but not one that could ever conceivably have been fulfilled because of the limit of weapons that were available at the time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This entry then goes on: "Other things: We need to be positioned well, organised. Friendly and family connections are not enough." I can as a -- "I can help as a friend or a relative, but I cannot make someone else do the same." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, was this something that you understood to be the position at that time, that really it wasn't possible without some sort of central command for orders to be issued that would be obeyed?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, it goes without saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just so that the Judges understand that. I mean, the people who were members of the KLA on the ground, the people you'd been visiting, many of them were farmers by day and might volunteer for the KLA one day and be back on their farms the next. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During that period, that was the case in some areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So any difficult order that might be issued would be quite hard to implement?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Essentially, no commander could rely on the commitment of a group of civilians who from time to time would pick up arms and man a check-point, could they? They couldn't rely on them?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I want to look now at the next entry against the name "Nazmi." And I think you know Nazmi Brahimaj, don't you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And we see him listed as one of those present at the meeting. Nazmi Brahimaj is recorded as saying: "I fully support this," which, I think, you will agree seems to be a reference to the proposal for the creation of a single command. "I fully support this." But then he says this: "The Dukagjin Staff has presented us with a fait accompli but otherwise" - something - "and we" are -- I'm sorry, "we were in agreement that day." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's plain, is it not, that at that stage Brahimajs who were based in Jablanica did not regard themselves as being part of the Dukagjin Staff because he's referring to the Dukagjin Staff presenting this meeting with a fait accompli?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Nazmi. He's from Jablanica. But I am not seeing here whether it was earlier on part of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. If you just drop down a few lines there's two entries against the name of Ramush Haradinaj. And then there's an entry against the name of Lahi, and it says: "We are in favour of ..." and then "unanimously." "Unanimously all are," and then some words crossed out, "in favour of form -- and announcing the formation for the announcement of the staff of the plain of Dukagjin." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So I suggest to you that reading these minutes as a whole, what we see is that first resolution that a single unified staff for the plain of Dukagjin should be created there on the 23rd of June. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the meeting then moves on to discuss the appointment of the staff, and Salih, S-a-l-i-h, makes a proposal. Do you know -- I think you've already told us you know who Salih Veseli is. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so his proposal is that the staff should have a commander, a deputy or assistant commander for morale and politics, a Chief of Staff, an assistant for logistics, for intelligence, and counter-intelligence. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that proposal appears to have been approved, do you see that, immediately afterwards?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And we then move on to the election of who those people should be. Sorry. Pause for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We then move on in the meeting to the election of who those people should be, and the next entry records Mr. Haradinaj suggesting, and I quote: "It would have been good if representatives of each of the subzone staffs were recruited as members to the operational staff of Dukagjin." Then Nazmi is recorded as saying: "People have to know what the operational zones are." And then Salih Veseli is recorded as saying: "I propose that the commander be a fighter who has been fighting so far with success." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then Rrustem Teta makes the proposal: "I propose Ramush Haradinaj ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then a little lower down there's a reference to somebody called Agron. Do you see that, just a couple of lines down, just immediately after the entry you've just been looking at? The line begins: "Agron," and then there is a colon. Do you see that? You need to answer, I'm afraid, on the transcript, rather than nodding. Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to suggest to you from the context that it becomes clear, both in this minute and the other one of this meeting, that Agron must be one of the members of the General Staff or at least a representative of the General Staff. Was Agron a nickname that you were familiar with or have ever been familiar with?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I don't know of anyone called Agron in the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, of course, people don't always use their full names, do they?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, they mostly used nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of Rexhep Selimi using the nickname Agron?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. To my recollection, his nickname was Dhjeteshi.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Agron refers to Lahi and says: "Lahi was the representative of the central staff of the plain of Dukagjin. Perhaps this was a secret. The staff has been in existence from 1993 until now." Can I ask you about this: As far as you understood it, was there a period of time where even the commanders on the ground didn't know who was in the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that period because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then Mr. Haradinaj is referred to in the immediately following entry: "Commander Ramush: The central staff is not providing us with the orders that we require; it is absent." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think you've agreed that that's a pretty fair reflection of the reality on the ground, don't you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for that period in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the minute then moves to the process of election, electing who should lead the command. Ramush proposes, as we see just a few lines down, Ramush says: "I am in favour of Lahi being commander; Salih Veseli, the deputy; and Rrustem the assistant." Do you see that? It's just about six lines further down.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it appears that Ramush Haradinaj was nominating Lahi Brahimaj as the commander of the zone; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then Agron is recorded as saying: "Draft what your views are and the KLA General Staff will respond in two days." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then Salih Veseli says: "Who is in favour of Ramush as commander, Lahi as deputy, Salih as Chief of Staff, and Rrustem as deputy?" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then a second proposal is put with the difference that Ramush and Lahi change places. Do you see that immediately underneath?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then the votes of the commanders from the different areas are recorded. For the first proposal, that is Ramush as commander: "Jablanica, Reka in favour of Ramush, Baran valley." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then for Lahi as commander: Gllogjan and Leshan valley. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Leshan valley, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you have a situation in which the Jablanica commands are recommending that Ramush should be the commander, whilst the Gllogjan command, including Ramush Haradinaj, are recommending that Lahi should be the commander. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then the decision is recorded by a vote. It was decided by vote that Ramush Haradinaj would be the commander, Lahi his deputy, Salih the Chief of Staff - as you, yourself, said, I think - Rrustem the deputy. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then immediately after that, Salih Veseli, who you've told us had some past military experience, gave a clarification of what the tasks of a commander would be. Do you see that, immediately underneath the vote? It says: "Subsequently at a question by Ramush, Salih Veseli," and gave a professional clarification of the tasks of a commander, the deputy, and Chief of Staff. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it's clear, is it not, that this was a process of election, first of all. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Attended by villages which had been operating autonomously up until then but are trying to come together in a single command?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It culminates in a vote in favour of Ramush Haradinaj as the commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At which point, he immediately turns to one person who has military experience and asks him, What should a commander do? What should the roles and responsibilities be?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I'm not going to go in the same detail into the other record of this meeting, but it is right that Your Honours should be aware of it. Could we please bring up -- I'm sorry, just one moment - P142, I'm told, is the reference for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not in your yellow binder, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's not, in fact, no, but it says -- it's -- I think, first of all, could you -- could you just -- could I ask that the usher scroll down gently at the witness's -- following the witness's eye, just to give him an opportunity to familiarise himself with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, it's not in the binder, I'm afraid. But if you could look at it on the screen and then give the usher a nod every now and again. And I don't need you to read every word, because it follows exactly the same order as the minute we've just been looking at. It's in somewhat greater detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do Your Honours have the English translation on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Actually, we have the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. The English translation is linked to it, but they can't both be at the screen at the same time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If they are properly linked, then, Mr. Emmerson, we -- we have access in court to our own system.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do Your Honours -- it might be helpful to have the English version on the screen, because there were just two passages I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's a matter of fact that I have it at least on one of my screens at this moment. Yes. So please proceed, even if --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is -- this is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if you might just put it down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is a much more detailed typed minute of the same meeting, I think, Mr. Zyrapi, and you've, in fact, looked at it before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, it's the minutes of meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I simply want to ask you about two points, please -- I'm sorry, three points altogether. Much of the language is the same, although it is more detailed in places.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we turn, please, on the English translation to page 2, and in the Albanian to the first reference to the name of Nazmi, which should be on -- at the bottom of page 2 of the Albanian version, just so that we can see a slightly clearer record of what Nazmi was saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you see that at the bottom there? Our translation of that reads, and this is following the proposal for the creation of a single staff: "I fully agree with this, yet the Dukagjini Staff has placed before us a done deal, otherwise I agree." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then a little further down --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If we could just turn to the second page -- sorry, the following page of the Albanian. In the English, it's just a little further down on page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In heavy type, do you have there: "It was unanimously decided and the formation of the Dukagjin Plain Operative Staff was proclaimed." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we go to the next bullet -- heavy bullet point there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which in our English translation is at the top of page 3, but it appears on the screen that we have it in the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The next decision: "Unanimously decided for the staff to have its commander, deputy-commander, assistant for morale and politics, Chief of Staff, logistics assistant, and assistant for intelligence and counter-intelligence." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then you have the same process of election nomination -- or rather, nomination and election taking place. And at the very end, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we -- could we go to the very end of this minute. So it's the -- page 4 of the English translation and page 3 of the Albanian translation. I think that's still not the right page of the Albanian -- I'm sorry, it is correct page of the Albanian translation. I apologise. Page 4 of the English translation. The last decision is the appointment of ten people for different military branches of service in the Dukagjin area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then Agroni again: "I would like to explain that you can be called the Dukagjini Plain Local Operative Staff, taking into consideration the KLA division into zones." Following which there is an entry against the name Smajl, S-m-a-j-l, and I think you said before that that is a name that you knew Mr. Haradinaj as; is that correct? That's your evidence?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "We should see if there is a possibility to re-define operative zones since the Dukagjin Staff encompasses a larger surface than the local staff." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, despite that meeting having taken place on the 23rd of June, you've told us that in the middle of July, the area to the west of the Peje to Gjakove road was still not incorporated into the zone. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember, that's why I went there to that zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you gave evidence about this minute in the Milutinovic case, Mr. Zyrapi, and I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For the record, the reference is 5939, lines -- lines 5 and following.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you said this: "In this document you can see that the staff of the operational area of Dukagjin is being formed." And then a little later, you said: "This has to do with the development of the Dukagjini Staff, and later on they speak about how the command of the operational zone would look like in the future." Again, can I ask you to confirm that that was your evidence and understanding?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, there's one thing that's not entirely clear to me yet, and let me ask the witness. We earlier saw the line where Nazmi in this 23rd of June meeting says: "I fully agree with this, yet the Dukagjini Staff has placed us before a done deal, otherwise I agree." It looks as if the Dukagjini Staff imposes its will on the formation of what now, as I understand, will be the Dukagjini Operational Zone. Now, who then exactly was the Dukagjini Staff that could impose its will on those present? I see that they come from different areas. I see Jablanica, Reka, Baran valley, Gllogjan, Leshan valley. Who then exactly is the Dukagjini Staff that presents, as it's called, a "done deal"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how things were at this period, but from what I see here, it's Dukagjin Operational Staff, which in this case is represented by Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what you say is it's actually the Gllogjan Staff which then enlarges the area, the operational area, to other areas as well, but what is here called the Dukagjini Staff, you said is the Gllogjan Staff. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After meetings held even earlier and documents were looked at, there were meetings with other staffs, with other village staffs, and the villages started to merge into a command, a single command. This is at least what I guessed from these documents because I wasn't there at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're interpreting the documents, but was this meeting on the basis of equality with the others or was the Dukagjini Staff or, as you said that was actually the Gllogjan Staff, were they imposing their will on the other village staffs as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we are talking about this meeting, there are other staffs present apart from Dukagjin, like Leshan and other villages. They have come together there to make a decision on the formation of an operational staff of Dukagjin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But was that a merger or was that expanding power over other village staffs? I'm trying to understand what exactly the Dukagjini Staff has imposed or, as it says, "has placed us before a done deal," which suggests that the Dukagjini Staff had a final say in what would happen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what I see here, it was a merger of local staffs into a single command. I don't know what he means by what he says here, because I wasn't there present to give you an accurate representation of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, this raised the issue of whether this witness is telling us on what happened at the time or whether he interprets for us --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that he remove his headphones so I can address Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you speak any English? Do you understand any English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you speak any French?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Not sufficient. I mean, I'm not overly concerned -- if the witness removes his headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you, please, take off your headphones. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm slightly surprised by the way that Your Honour characterised that entry in the questions that you've put to the witness because what is clear from a reading of these minutes as a whole is that all zones were represented and the decision to create a single over-arching zone was unanimously decided by all of them. And so, Your Honour, several times, used the expression was the Dukagjin Staff imposing its will, by reference to the fact that Nazmi Brahimaj is recorded as saying that a done deal had been placed before them, and of course, Nazmi Brahimaj would have been a representative of one area, namely Jablanica -- or one of the people present, rather, from Jablanica. But reading these minutes as a whole, it is our submission, quite plain, that this was a democratic decision taken -- and an election in which far from there being an imposed will, the Gllogjan command proposed a representative from Jablanica to be the commander and vice versa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand your surprise, but at the same time it was not without reasons that I put the question and that I not -- let's leave it for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have put the questions to the witness. I might have additional questions at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The other matter I just wanted to clarify, if I could, with Your Honour briefly, is this. Your Honour may recall from the Defence pre-trial brief - and I touched upon it briefly, very briefly in opening - that the Defence case is that at the end of May there was the formation of a small group of villages coming together calling themselves the Dukagjin Staff in the area around Gllogjan. And that it was at the 23rd of June that an attempt was made to create the operational plain, which then incorporated both Jablanica on the east and, in theory, Junik and the areas on the west of the road. So I just wanted to make that clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. That's clear. Please proceed. The witness has his ears -- his earphones on again. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if you could look now behind tab 5. This -- it does not, I think, yet have an exhibit number -- oh, it doesn't apparently now. It's Exhibit P145 I'm told?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We're now referring to the provisionally assigned numbers by Madam Registrar, so we'll come to that later. It's 145. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to look at the level of military sophistication that followed that meeting in -- on the 23rd of June so that we have a sense of the attempts that were then being made to introduce some military organisation. This is a minute of the newly formed Dukagjini Operative Staff the following day, the 24th of June, with everybody now with their ranks or positions recorded. And if we just look after the agenda, you see the seven agenda points there, Mr. Zyrapi. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There's then an introduction by Ramush Haradinaj in the minutes. Ramush Haradinaj said that: "Information regarding our forces and the forces of the enemy should be gathered. The enemy forces in Decane up to 200 men in strength." And then a little further down, just two lines down, the Chief of Staff, Mr. Veseli, begins to explain the idea of military planning and systemisation and the assaulting operations that should be undertaken. And do you see that there's then an entry that says the Chief of Staff then continued with the presentation of a training plan? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then there are various things listed that might be included within a training plan. And do you see about five bullet points down: "Five full hours soldier in attack"? Do you see that entry?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to get some idea of the military sophistication of this -- just going over the page. First of all: "Prepare them yourself or recall things. One tactical suggestion at once. Sir, the enemy is attacking from this direction. Work on soldiers' behaviour during an artillery attack. What a soldier does during an artillery attack." And then this: "Runs a hundred metres as fast as possible. Relocates himself until he receives correction. Repeat the hundred metres five times. Stop the column and analyse it." Now, pausing there, it seems, does it not, that the training is going to involve the suggestion that in the event of an artillery attack, you run as far as you can as fast as you can?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is that one of the features of being a fledgling guerilla organisation rather than a proper army? Would you see a direction to soldiers to run as far as they could and as fast as they could in the instructions in a proper army?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- these things are taught also in a regular army.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does a regular army have the ability to fire back at artillery positions?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At this stage in June, the KLA in Dukagjin had no ability to fire back at Serbian artillery, did they?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I now want to move a little further in time to one or two events that occurred shortly before you arrived. Could you look behind tab 6, first of all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, tab 6 is P161 provisionally assigned number.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And with a translation, I think, linked to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This document, Mr. Zyrapi, is dated the 4th of July and signed by Ramush Haradinaj. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it is a reprimand to Lahi Brahimaj. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it reads as follows: "Following our request for a working meeting that due to your absence from the zone of responsibility to which you belong, failed to take place twice in a row, we address to you this reprimand from us, requesting you to carry out your work faithfully. We ask for this behaviour not to be repeated." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then if you could just turn behind the following tab, tab 7?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tab 7 is P168, provisionally assigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is then, do you agree, an order dated the following day, the 5th of July, signed by Ramush Haradinaj. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Discharging Lahi Brahimaj from his position as deputy commander and appointing Nazmi Brahimaj in his place. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So on the face of it, it appears that Lahi Brahimaj was deputy commander in all for a period of about two weeks, would you agree, slightly less than two weeks?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From these documents, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you in the light of that about a comment that you made in your November 2005 statement at paragraph 19. I'll just read it into the record. You said: "Brahimaj," and you were referring then to Lahi Brahimaj, "Brahimaj had previously been the commander of the Dukagjini Zone, but the majority of the General Staff agreed that he was not up to the task and that RH was better suited to the job. Brahimaj was thus given a job in the General Staff as director of the finance department, and what could normally be seen as a promotion in a regular army was, in fact, a demotion." Do you see that? That was the -- that's a -- me reading to you a passage from your 2005 witness statement. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There are a number of things about that I want to suggest to you that are not entirely accurate as a summary. First of all, you say in that statement that Lahi Brahimaj had previously been the commander of the Dukagjini Zone, but the majority of the General Staff thought that Ramush was better suited to the job. Now, first of all, do you accept now that Lahi Brahimaj was never, in fact, commander of the Dukagjini Zone, but for two weeks was deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave the statement on the basis of what I heard when I took the task, but I'm not saying that I was present there and that I had proper information about everything that happened before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. But it's very important, you understand, Mr. Zyrapi, if you're giving this Tribunal evidence about command structures and who was responsible to whom, that you don't say things in witness statements about who was answerable to whom at a particular time if you don't know that that was the position. And there's a categorical statement in your 2005 witness statement that Lahi Brahimaj had been commander of the Dukagjini Zone, and I think you now accept that that statement is wrong; correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave the statement in 2005 based on what I was informed when I took over my duty as director of the operational directorate by the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you told us -- or you confirmed for me a little while ago that your visits to all these areas were very short and that, as you had said in previous testimony, your understanding of the command structures and who was responsible to who was incomplete. Is that a fair assessment of the position?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, especially in the case of Dukagjin Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so. And you've given some evidence today on oath to the Tribunal about who was in command of whom and which units in the Dukagjini Zone when you visited. Do we understand the same comment applies to that, that you could be mistaken about some of the evidence you've given?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about my testimony that Lahi was a commander, I have stated in my statement that this is what I was informed of by the staff; namely, that he was a commander in the past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the question of Mr. Emmerson, Mr. Zyrapi, is the following: In your statement, it says he was the commander, now you say that's what they told me, whether that was true or not now. Now, what Mr. Emmerson asks you is whether the limited knowledge you gained during your short visits, whether that could have caused similar mistakes in respect of other parts of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I hesitate to interrupt. It's not my turn yet. But I have noticed there's a very, very subtle distinction and it may be an important one. The witness used the expression he learned that Lahi Brahimaj was "a commander." Indeed, in his original interview with the OTP, he used the expression "a commander." That got itself translated into his original statement as "the commander," and it may well be that this is the source of the confusion. I hope that may help to clarify matters a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This, of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps -- now we have to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't really clarify the particular point I'm asking about, because what in the statement he says is Brahimaj had previously been the commander of the Dukagjin -- leaving that aside, he then goes on to say that the majority of the General Staff agreed that he was not up to the task, and RH was better suited to the job. In other words, the suggestion is, in the statement, that the General Staff decided that the job that Mr. Haradinaj subsequently did was one that Mr. Brahimaj was not up to and that does not seem to be in accordance with any of the material that we've looked at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would say give it some thought over the break, Mr. Emmerson. We need a break anyhow at this moment. We'll resume at five minutes past 1.00, but before adjourning, could we hear from you how much more time you would need? Because yesterday I praised the Prosecution for staying in the time-limits, where I usually praise the Defence for doing so, it seems now to be a bit different.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I rather thought that our time was not under huge pressure because of the structure -- in terms of sitting times because of the structure of the week. But I mean, I shall certainly finish in the next session. I would like to say I'll finish in about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but even then other counsel need time for cross-examination as well, there might be some questions from the Judges, so time pressure starts building up already. But -- so, therefore, you are advised -- all Defence counsel and Prosecution is advised that never start from the position that time pressure is any less because it's constantly there. We'll resume at five minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, I just want to conclude that question -- that line of questioning with you very briefly. The passage from your witness statement that I put to you could create the impression that it was the General Staff who had made the decision as to who should be the commander, and the General Staff who had removed Lahi Brahimaj from the position. Do you accept, having now looked at the records, that the decision as to who should be commander and deputy commander of the Dukagjini Plain Operational Zone was taken by democratic decision, made by the representatives of the villages of the area rather than a decision imposed by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The problem with that question is that this witness says that he doesn't know, he wasn't there. So he's being asked -- if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Mr. Emmerson puts to the witness that on the basis of this document is, Has your opinion changed or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, we are not asking the witness to make any inferences from the document. Let's ask whether he has any knowledge about --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I'm challenging the suggestion in his statement that it was a decision made by the General Staff. Whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ask him how he knows that and when it took place, rather than to ask him to make -- to draw conclusions on the basis of the document because you referred him to the document as support for --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what has happened at any time. Please put the question in more factual terms than this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, is it your evidence that the decision as to who should be the zone commander and the deputy zone commander is a decision that was made by the General Staff or not?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated then, I was told and explained the things that I said in the statement. But I was not given details about how that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And who told you?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was Rexhep Selimi and other members of the staff who told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know how they knew what the workings of the meeting had been?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Similarly, as to the removal of Lahi Brahimaj, is it your evidence that that was a decision taken by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. When I went and joined the General Staff, I found him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you don't know one way or the other whether the decision to remove him was a decision made by Ramush Haradinaj or by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I want to turn now to - and reasonably briefly - to the visit that you paid to Gllogjan in mid-July. Can I understand, first of all, that was the first time you'd been to anywhere in the Dukagjini region during 1998. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The second occasion, I think you told us, was sometime in August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And apart from those two occasions, were you in Dukagjin at all during the -- during 1998?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the visit in July involved one day in Jablanica, one day in the Gllogjan area, and one day east of the main road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in your April 2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just to correct the transcript, I'm sure it's a -- just a minor matter, but it -- the area is west, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right. I think it was me that was in error. One day west of the main road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In your April 2007 statement at paragraph 29, you say this, and I quote: "Towards the end of June or early July, I heard that Ramush Haradinaj was commander of the Dukagjini Operational Zone." As far as you can now recall, was it, in fact, at the end of June or early July that you first heard that he had been appointed as commander of the Dukagjini Operational Zone?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, that was the period. I'm not sure whether it was the end of one month or the beginning of the other, but that's the period when I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And by the time you went to Jablanica in mid-July, Lahi Brahimaj had already been removed from his position as deputy commander, is that correct, as far as you understood the position?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went there mid-July, Lahi was member of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. He was no longer the deputy commander of the Dukagjini Plain Operational Zone by that time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I made that visit, he was member of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you answer my question, Mr. Zyrapi? By the time you made that visit, he was not deputy commander of the zone, was he?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, that's correct, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you conducted a tour around the area in Jablanica on the occasion of that first day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you looked at various positions in the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can I ask you to confirm a passage from the evidence that you gave in the Milutinovic case at page 6239, line 7, where you said that: "During the time I visited the positions and the units in that area, I didn't come across a detention facility." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you some questions about the second day, if I may, and the time that you spent in the area around Gllogjan. First of all, in your April 2007 statement, at paragraph 37, and also in your 2005 statement, at paragraph 23, you list the names of certain individuals who you say were commanders in particular villages. So, for example, you suggest that Driton Zeneli was a subzone commander in Jablanica, and you suggest that Maliq Ndrecaj was a subzone commander in Prilep. I want to suggest to you that you are wrong about that information and that, for example, at the time of your visit, those two individuals -- Driton Zeneli, first of all, was based in Gllogjan and not in Jablanica; and Maliq Ndrecaj was the subzone commander for Carabreg and not for Prilep. Is it possible that you could be mistaken about who was the subzone commander for each of these villages and have become confused in that visit?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. I met Driton in Jablanica when I went there. I visited Maliq in Prilep -- Prilep and Carabreg are very close to each other, and maybe he was in different place at the time. But as far as I remember, I went and met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sure you met these individuals, but you've recorded in your statement that they are subzone commanders for particular villages, and I think you now accept that those records that you've made may be in error. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it could be, although it's been a long time, as you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Secondly then, if I may, in that respect, could I ask that you be shown on the ELMO an aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we pull it back so that both of the crosses marked on that photograph can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, pausing there. Mr. Zyrapi, I have marked those two crosses on the photograph because I'm suggesting to you that those were the locations at which the large machine-guns that you saw were, in fact, located. And just to help you with your orientation, if you look towards the left-hand side of the picture just below and to the left of the first cross on the left, that is the crossroads at the centre of Gllogjan.
