And I suggest to you that the first of the machine-guns you saw was located on the road that leads from that junction towards Shaptej. And that the second was located in the position marked on the right-hand side of the photograph very close to the Haradinaj family compound on the road in from Dubrave. Now, first of all, you are obviously marking positions on a very large or -- possibly the opposite way, a very small-scale map, the approximate locations. Do you accept that the precise locations may have been the positions that I show in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my visit, especially here to this crossroads, there was a 12.5-millimetre machine-gun -- 12.7 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- but I don't know whose houses these were.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm simply inviting you to confirm that the precise locations were as I have marked them on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one here in the upper part of the photograph was on the road, while the second one was close to the houses, but I don't know whose houses those were. I just visited the place, the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Is the position this, that you can't say one way or the other whether the crosses I've marked are accurate?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. The guns that you saw were 1950s models, weren't they? They were elderly weapons?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were anti-aircraft machine-guns, 12.7, Chinese make.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you look behind tab --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, perhaps the witness could answer the question. It wasn't what the make was, whether they are 1950s models. I think that needs to be addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I thought the first word of the answer did address it, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you, Mr. Zyrapi, can you confirm, please, that the weapons that you saw were elderly weapons?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, old makes, but they functioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. They functioned -- they were the sort of things that were used as anti-aircraft weapons in the Second World War. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were elderly weapons, as you said, but I don't know whether they were used during the Second World War. I could see for myself that they were old weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you turn, please, behind tab 12 of the bundle. You should have a map behind tab 12, at the very end of the bundle. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is a map produced by the colonel in charge of the Serb forces in that area, showing the deployment of Serb forces in the area to the south-west -- sorry, south-east of Gllogjan during the period between April and September 1998. Now, you gave certain evidence yesterday about Serb positions on the main road, and then followed that up by suggesting that there were no Serb positions on the interior of the countryside? And if you look at the red line that -- on that map is preceding from the direction of the top left-hand corner town towards Gjakove, that is the main road from Peje to Gjakove. And I want to suggest to you that there were Serb artillery and combined Serb forces positions at the south end of Lake Radoniq and at three elevated positions: A hill near Baballoq; a hill called Radonjicka Suka or Donji Bites immediately west to the Lake Radoniq; and a hill called Suka Cermjan to the east of Lake Radoniq.

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the map, and when I explained my movements in the Dukagjini area, I explained where I passed and the positions of the Serbs at that time. I did not go to the other areas because of restrictions of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, but you also gave evidence that there was no Serb -- there were no Serb positions located within the -- I think the word you used was "hinterland," but certainly within the countryside areas. And I'm suggesting to you that that evidence that you gave yesterday is wrong and that there were Serb positions, both at the south of Lake Radoniq and on each of the three hills that I have described to you, Mr. Zyrapi. Can I ask you, please, to indicate what your response to that suggestion is?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also said that in the statement and repeated it in my testimony, that I only indicated the places where I've been and where I knew that there were Serb positions. I don't know about other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Listen carefully to the question, Mr. Zyrapi, and then answer it if you will. You gave evidence yesterday that there were no Serb positions in the countryside to the east of the main road. I want to put to you the suggestion in clear terms that that evidence was wrong and that there were Serb positions mounted on the elevated areas I've described and at the south of Lake Radoniq and, indeed, that just a short while, a matter of two weeks or less after you were there, the British Military Attache observed four hours of heavy shelling from that position. I want to ask you, please, to respond to the suggestion that the evidence, that you gave yesterday, was in error.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, if Your Honours please, that question's unfair because the line of questioning is certainly quite proper, I've got no problem with that. But surely we should elicit from this witness what he means when he talks about the hinterland and the area to the east. He said that he hadn't been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's look first exactly at what he said yesterday. Mr. Emmerson, could you guide me --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I apologise. I don't have the reference to my -- to hand. But certainly when asked to locate, in answer to questions from Mr. Di Fazio, the Serb positions, the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he use the word "hinterland" or --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: He did. I remember it. It was my question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be easy to find. It will be easy to find. One second, please. At least if it's ... I've got it on page 3240.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does the answer say: "When I toured Prilep village, the road was -- which goes to Decane-Gjakove was nearby and the Serbian forces had taken up positions there but not in the hinterland of the villages"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly -- that's really what is on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. The question I'm putting to the witness, if I can be clear about it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- is that there were, in fact, Serb positions, very substantial Serb artillery and combined forces positions on the locations I've described on the east of the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zyrapi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, Mr. Emmerson, we have to be careful. We have to understand a question in relation to the -- in relation -- we have to understand the answer in relation to the question. The question was: "In the time that you were touring during this tour of three days, other than the Serb positions that you've mentioned, did you encounter any other Serb positions?"

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand the answer to be that where the witness was moving around, that he did not encounter, even if literally the answer may have been of a more absolute character, nevertheless, we should first try to better understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the evidence before we say that it was wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not in the process of seeking to criticise the witness but seeking to clarify exactly what the position is, because that on the face of it appears to be a categorical statement, but I'm very happy for the witness to clarify the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zyrapi, were you or were you not aware that there were Serb artillery positions to the west -- I'm sorry, to the east of the main road when you visited?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were artillery Serb positions in Podi i Geshtenjave there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Where are you indicating?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a part where you leave Decane in the direction of Peje. It's a place called Podi i Geshtenjave there. This is where the Serb artillery position was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help us on the map, please, where you say this was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps let's first try to find out. Witness, could you tell us, is that north of Decani or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you go west, in the direction of Peje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But is there --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is it north-west of Decani or is it -- if we have the road that starts from Peje and then to Decani and then to Gjakove, is it on the Peje to Decani stretch, or on the Decani to Gjakove stretch that you're describing?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the stretch Decane-Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's -- that's -- I think, the area you're describing, correct me if I'm wrong, is on the west side of the main road near Decane, is that correct? On the border side of the main road?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the main road that goes from Decane to Peje, if you are asking me about the Serb artillery position.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. Let -- just pause there for a moment. The question I'm asking you, which I hope is reasonably clear, Mr. Zyrapi, is that there were Serb artillery and combined forces positions located on the high ground to the east of the main road around the area of Lake Radoniq, on both sides of it. Now, if -- can you please indicate to us in clear terms whether you can confirm or deny, or you do not know?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I only spoke about places where I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, then let me put it to you this way: You're not in a position, are you, to confirm that there were no Serb forces stationed in the countryside to the east of the main Peje to Gjakove road? You're not in a position to confirm that there were no Serb forces stationed on the east side in the countryside?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I gave the statement, I spoke only about the places where I went, which I visited, and where I didn't see such positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If Your Honour's happy that that is a clear enough answer to the question, then I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But before doing so, this map is -- it says it's -- it's tendered and admitted, in which case do you want this to be assigned a number?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, because that is a map which will be -- which is in the bundle which was shown to Colonel Crosland, and so it will be assigned a number through that mechanism. That's Colonel Delic's map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It doesn't sound, Mr. Zyrapi, if I may say so, as if you got a very clear picture of where the Serb forces were located in the Dukagjin region. Would you accept that suggestion?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I could surmise from my movements. In general, as I said, I didn't see Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just one other topic, if I may, please, from that part of your visit. How long did you spend in Irzniq altogether?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the accurate time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, just give us an indication, if you would, please. You visited quite a number of different locations before lunch, didn't you? Just tell us how much time you spent in Irzniq, approximately?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you an estimate. I really don't remember the accurate time I spent there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could it have been less than half an hour?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could. I know that we stayed there for a short time, at least this is what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could it have been less than 15 minutes?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. More than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it's at least 15 minutes, but it could be less than half an hour?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be precise, really. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You mentioned rapid intervention units. Were you aware of rapid intervention units in other parts of Kosovo at this time?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the time when they started to be formed. They were in Drenica Zone because of the need to give assistance to go to the secourse of other units along the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can you help us about this: In the process of the emerging structures that you've described, where villages were coming together and were beginning to try to form Joint Commands, in general terms, do you know when in that that process the rapid intervention units started to be formed?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you a precise time, but from what I know in Drenica Zone, I think they started to be formed in June or July, but I couldn't give you an accurate estimation of time for other zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Taking these different rapid intervention units together, do you know if it was somebody's idea to form them, to have rapid intervention units in general? Was it someone's suggestion as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Drenica, when I went there, I suggested to them to form such rapid intervention units to be ready to intervene when they were called upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So in Drenica, at least, you've got some idea of when it was formed, is that right, and how it was formed?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was it your suggestion in Dukagjin as well?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suggested this in Drenice. I didn't have contacts in Dukagjin.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know when the Dukagjin Rapid Intervention Unit was formed?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know whose idea it was to form it?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know where in the Dukagjini area it was first formed?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know where its operational area was; in other words, how wide it could move?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know whether it had more than one base?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only -- I know only when I visited where I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, you've given us certain evidence about rapid intervention units being under the direct command of zone commanders, but I want to suggest to you, just so that it's clear, that rapid intervention units had the capacity to act completely on their own initiative, without instructions?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, they were under the command of the zone commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is that based on your experience in Drenica?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because the only time you spent looking at anybody from a rapid intervention unit in Dukagjin was the half an hour or however long it was that you were in Irzniq. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know how much independence or autonomy there was for the rapid intervention unit in the Dukagjini area, to what extent they could make their own decisions about deployment?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In your November 2005 statement at paragraphs 24 to 25, you make some comments about this. And in paragraph 25, you say: "Toger's unit was not attached to any particular subzone. They could operate anywhere in the Dukagjini area." What was the basis for that comment? Where did you get that information from?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made this comment based on what I knew of rapid intervention units in other zones, and when I visited it they had a special command and a special place they were in.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see. But as you've told us a moment ago you don't know whether they had other locations elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: BISLIM ZYRAPI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Penultimate topic, if I may, the second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say "penultimate topic." Mr. Emmerson, I think it's fair that you would conclude with the witness during this session, which we've only a couple of minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, in those circumstances, there's no point in me embarking on a further topic. The witness went to Dukagjin on a second occasion and dealt with, he said in his witness statement, an incident concerning the relationship between FARK and the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps a practical solution might be if you confer with some of your colleagues, who still have some remaining time for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, except that neither of them are concerned with that part of the case, but I'll leave it if Your Honour's of that view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can't pursue it if there isn't time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time -- at the same time, you gave an indication --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might interject. If I -- if I could get some guidance from the Chamber as to how much more time the Chamber envisions we will be with this particular witness, perhaps a conference between the three of us may be of some assistance; then again it may not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the next witness, which is Witness 29, the OTP has asked for two and a half hours, and on the basis of the assumption that they are as disciplined as they were with this witness, that means that tomorrow we would have one session and a half, approximately, for -- a little bit less for this witness. Earlier, I don't exactly remember what you said earlier, Mr. Guy-Smith, but how much time would you under the present circumstances -- how much time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, my -- my time is less than it had been before, and I think -- I think it's fair to say substantially less. But what I can say is this: With regard to the upcoming witness, I expect to be spending very little time with that witness, based upon the manner in which I believe the evidence will be led. And I'm confident that we can finish both this witness as well as the next witness's examination-in-chief, using both the balance of today, if I sit down rapidly, as well as tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, let's just look at -- Mr. Di Fazio -- let me first ask Mr. Harvey, how much time would you still need? Mr. Guy-Smith, if you say, I need less time than I assessed before, could you give us -- I mean, "less," could be one minute less or half an hour less.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I figure that I will probably be somewhere in the neighbourhood of between 15 or 20 minutes. It could be shorter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I think I'm going to be between 20 minutes and half an hour with this witness, Your Honour. I will have no questions for the witness tomorrow, if I that assists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just taking stock of the position overall, Thursday is set aside for cross-examination alone of the following witness and re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think I'm right in saying that I will be conducting almost all of the cross-examination of tomorrow's witness on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You asked for additional time on the 5th of February for Witness 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, exactly so. I can't imagine that I would need anything more in total than two hours for Witness 29. It's a confined single incident, event. And so on any view, even if Witness 29's evidence did not conclude tomorrow in chief, I would be confident that we would complete cross-examination of Witness 29 and re-examination before the end of Thursday's session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So to that extent -- and I'm sorry if I made certain assumptions about how the week was organised when I was planning cross-examination of witness, but it did seem to me that he had, particularly by reference to the documents that he has been asked to look at, some information that might assist the Trial Chamber on some of the structural questions, which would take a little time to go through. And I do apologise, I should have notified you earlier that I thought it would take rather longer than I thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, Witness 29 has been scheduled for two and a half hours, but I think at the time there was no issue of 92 ter yet. We -- what's the present assessment of how much time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, I've been speaking to Mr. Kearney, who's going to have the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And he's not alerted me to any substantial increase in the -- in the allocated time. If Your Honours please, I can try and find out and give you a more accurate indication, but certainly -- and I've spoken to him a little bit about -- about the witness, and there's nothing that he's said to me - and I would have expected him to -

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- to indicate that there's a particular problem or that the estimate is -- is wildly wrong or there's some inaccuracy in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us an indication as -- as the matters stand now how much time you would need for --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Yes. Thank you. Mr. Kearney is listening to us, and he informs us that he will need, as he puts it, every second of 2.5 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear. Now, as matters stand now, how much time you would need for re-examination of the present witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: As matters stand now, about 15 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 15 or 20 minutes, which means that if the Defence tomorrow, and I think that could be -- should be possible to achieve that during the first session, that the Defence would finish cross-examination, would then perhaps have a few questions from the Bench. And then by the middle of the second session tomorrow, we might finish with this witness and start the examination-in-chief. And in view of what we heard from Mr. Emmerson, even if the examination-in-chief could not be fully completed on Wednesday, that would not have any dramatic results. Is this of sufficient guidance?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then first of all, Mr. Zyrapi, we'd like to see you back tomorrow, again 9.00 in the morning, same courtroom. I'll now ask Madam Usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A request was made for further protective measures in respect of Witness 29. The Chamber was informed that the Defence does not object. Is that true for --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although I'll not give at this moment reasons for it, of course that will be done in public session, but the request is granted in respect of Witness 29. That means pseudonym was already in place, and face and voice distortion added to that. Then I'd like to thank the interpreters and technicians for their assistance today, and we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- will adjourn until the 25th of April, that is tomorrow, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 25th day of April, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.51 p.m.,
